latest_release.name: v1.1.3
latest_release.body:
### Documentation

* flet-notifications: Document how to update a notification after an inline reply on Android, and fix the "Action buttons and replies" example's notification staying stuck with a spinner after a reply ([#7058](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/discussions/7058), [#7060](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7060)) by @ItsRenjiii.
* Document how to show a loading screen while `main()` starts up, and where unhandled exceptions from handlers, tasks and threads end up, in the Async apps guide ([#7100](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/issues/7100), [#7101](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7101)) by @daneeller.

### Improvements

* flet-mcp knows flet-shadcn-ui's Lucide icons: `get_enum("LucideIcons")` and `enum_has_member()` list them, and `find_icon(query, family="lucide")` searches them (a search without a family still returns only Material and Cupertino icons). Its API reference now also covers flet-local-auth, flet-notifications and flet-spinkit ([#7118](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7118)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* flet-mcp records what each Flet module exports, the keyword arguments each class takes and each enum's members, introspected from the installed packages, so code checkers can catch `ft.PieChart` (it's `flet_charts.PieChart`), `ft.TextField(helper_text=...)` or `ft.Colors.BLACK45` before the code runs: `ApiStore.module_exports()`, `modules_exporting()`, `init_params()`, `settable_attrs()` and `module_enum_members()`, on the store the MCP server shares through `shared_api_store()` ([#7118](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7118)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* Load a `DataTable` of thousands of rows without freezing the app: a table with 100 or more rows of one height builds only the rows near the visible part of the page, so a 3,470-row table loads in one 0.2 s frame instead of a 4 s freeze, and selecting a row no longer freezes the app for a second; set the new `build_rows_on_demand` to `False` to build every row ([#7076](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7076)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* Load a `DataTable2` (`flet-datatable2`) of thousands of rows without freezing the app: a table with 100 or more rows builds only the rows near the visible part of the table, so a 3,470-row table loads in one 0.3 s frame instead of a 2.5 s freeze. `flet-datatable2` now carries its own copy of `data_table_2`'s `DataTable2` to do this, and honors `build_rows_on_demand` too ([#7076](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7076)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* Scroll long pages and tables smoothly: every control used to get its own compositing layer, so a page of thousands of controls, like a `DataTable` with thousands of rows, stuttered on every scroll frame; controls now add a layer only while their `opacity` is between 0 and 1, and a `DataTable` no longer repaints all of its rows as it scrolls ([#7076](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7076)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* Look up icons by name, as with enum members: `ft.Icons["HOME"]`, `ft.CupertinoIcons["ADD"]` and `LucideIcons[...]`, and check a name with `"HOME" in ft.Icons` ([#7114](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7114)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* `ft.use_dialog()` raises a `TypeError` for a dialog returned from an `@ft.component` function, or any other control that isn't a dialog, instead of silently never opening it ([#7114](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7114)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* Start web apps that use `flet-rive` 1 MB lighter when they don't show a `Rive` control: the Rive engine (`rive_native.wasm`) now loads when the first `Rive` control loads its file, instead of at startup ([#7057](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7057)) by @FeodorFitsner.

### Bug fixes

* Fix `DataTable.horizontal_lines` having no effect ([#7076](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/pull/7076)) by @FeodorFitsner.
* Fix event handlers and `use_effect` setups that call an async function from a plain function, such as `on_click=lambda: save(item)` or `ft.use_effect(lambda: load(item_id), [item

detail.readme:
Build cross-platform apps in Python. No frontend experience required.

Flet is a Python framework for building web, desktop, and mobile apps without prior experience in frontend development. > **[Try Flet online in Flet Studio](https://studio.flet.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=flet)** > > Create, run, and share Python apps in your browser. Start from an example, write your own code, or get help from the AI agent. No installation required. ###    One Python codebase, six platforms Build your interface and application logic in Python, and run your app on iOS, Android, Windows, macOS, Linux, and web. No Dart, Swift, Kotlin, HTML, or JavaScript required. ###    150+ built-in controls and services Create your interface with ready-made layouts, buttons, forms, navigation, and dialogs. Customize colors, typography, and themes, with Material and Cupertino controls to suit your app. ###    Declarative UI for growing apps Organize your app into reusable components and let the UI update when application state changes. Prefer changing controls directly? The imperative style is supported too. [Compare the approaches](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/declarative-vs-imperative). ###    Your Python libraries, on mobile Use libraries such as NumPy, pandas, Pillow, and cryptography in your mobile apps. Flet provides [prebuilt binary packages](https://pypi.flet.dev) for iOS and Android, so you don't have to compile native dependencies yourself. ###    Run in the browser or on your server Run Python directly in the browser with Pyodide and WebAssembly, with no Python server required. Or keep your Python code on a server and deliver real-time UI updates to the browser. ###    Built-in packaging Use `flet build` to package your app for desktop, mobile, or web distribution, including the App Store and Google Play. Configure dependencies, icons, and platform settings in your project's `pyproject.toml`. ###    Test your app on desktop and mobile Write [integration tests with pytest](https://flet.dev/docs/getting-started/integration-testing) and run them against your packaged app with `flet test`. Tap buttons, enter text, and verify user flows on desktop and mobile, with screenshot comparisons on Android and iOS. ###    Build with help from AI Explore and create apps with the AI agent in [Flet Studio](https://studio.flet.dev/?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=flet), or connect your coding assistant to the [Flet MCP server](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/flet-mcp) for version-specific API information and tools to find examples and icons. ###    Extensible Build custom controls in Python by composing existing controls, or create extensions that wrap Flutter packages to add new UI components and platform integrations. ###    Accessible Add screen-reader labels, tooltips, keyboard shortcuts, and custom semantics to help more people use your app. Inspect the accessibility information your UI exposes with the [semantics debugger](https://flet.dev/docs/cookbook/accessibility#debugging-semantics). ## Flet app example This simple counter app displays a number in the center of the screen. Press the **+** button to increment it: ```python import flet as ft def main(page: ft.Page): counter = ft.Text("0", size=50, data=0) def increment_click(e): counter.data += 1 counter.value = str(counter.data) page.floating_action_button = ft.FloatingActionButton( icon=ft.Icons.ADD, on_click=increment_click ) page.add( ft.SafeArea( expand=True, content=ft.Container( content=counter, alignment=ft.Alignment.CENTER, ), ) ) ft.run(main) ``` To run the app, install `flet`: ```bash pip install 'flet[all]' ``` Save the code as `counter.py`, then launch the app: ```bash flet run counter.py ``` This opens the app in a native desktop window. The screenshot below shows it after pressing **+** three times:

To run the same app in your browser, add `--web`: ```bash flet run --web counter.py ```

## Learn more * [Website](https://flet.dev) * [Documentation](https://flet.dev/docs/) * [Roadmap](https://flet.dev/roadmap) * [Apps Gallery](https://studio.flet.dev/gallery?utm_source=github&utm_medium=readme&utm_campaign=flet) ## Community * [Discussions](https://github.com/flet-dev/flet/discussions) * [Discord](https://discord.gg/dzWXP8SHG8) * [X (Twitter)](https://twitter.com/fletdev) * [Bluesky](https://bsky.app/profile/fletdev.bsky.social) * [Email us](mailto:hello@flet.dev) ## Contributing Want to help improve Flet? Check out the [contribution guide](CONTRIBUTING.md).
